Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only clinicians, low vision users, cognitive load-sensitive users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, keyboard-only navigation, screen magnifier **Feature:** Real-time notification panel with priority-tiered live regions in a hospital EHR application **Risk Level:** High (Patient safety implications, mixed-politeness live regions, auto-dismiss timing, complex focus management) **Component/Page Type:** Dynamic notification panel, badge trigger, dismiss interactions, history drawer, auto-dismiss control --- ## Scope & Context - **What is being built?** A collapsible notification panel triggered by a bell icon in the top navigation, displaying real-time WebSocket notifications across three priority tiers (Critical/Error, Warning, Info), with a persistent "Notification History" drawer and auto-dismiss functionality. - **User need:** Clinicians must receive immediate awareness of critical patient safety alerts without losing workflow context for lower-priority items. Lower-tier notifications should announce quietly or wait until the user is ready. - **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA (default), Section 508/ADA compliance required for medical EHR systems. - **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), keyboard-only users, screen magnifier users. - **Risk factors:** - Patient safety: Missing a Critical announcement is a clinical failure. - Mixed politeness levels: Cannot use a single `role="alert"` for all tiers. - Auto-dismiss timing: 10s/30s timeouts may violate WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable for AT users. - Existing code flaws: Silent badge updates, `` dismiss buttons, no landmark structure, no pause control. - **Constraints:** React SPA (TypeScript), WebSocket integration, must maintain existing visual design system, medical context requires explicit priority labeling and non-color indicators. --- ## Semantic Structure Plan Design the HTML structure and landmark regions to support screen reader navigation and dynamic state: 1. **Document structure & landmarks:** - `

``` --- ## Interaction Pattern Design ### Interactive Elements Table | Widget | APG Pattern | Keyboard Model | ARIA Attributes | WCAG Citation | |--------|-------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------| | Bell Trigger Button | Menu Button / Popover (APG) | Tab: focus button. Enter/Space: open panel. Escape: close panel. | `aria-expanded="false"`, `aria-controls="notification-panel"`, `aria-label="Notifications, X unread"` | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Notification Dismiss Button | Button (APG) | Tab: focus button. Enter/Space: dismiss notification. | `aria-label="Dismiss: [Priority] [Message Summary]"`, `aria-disabled="true"` (during async dismiss) | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Pause Auto-Dismiss Toggle | Toggle Button (APG) | Tab: focus button. Enter/Space: toggle pause state. | `aria-pressed="false"`, `aria-label="Pause auto-dismiss"` / `"Resume auto-dismiss"` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable | | History Drawer Trigger | Disclosure (APG) | Tab: focus button. Enter/Space: open drawer. Escape: close drawer. | `aria-expanded="false"`, `aria-controls="history-drawer"` | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Close Panel/History Buttons | Button (APG) | Tab: focus button. Enter/Space: close overlay/drawer. | `aria-label="Close [panel/drawer]"` | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | ### Live Region Architecture (Critical Design Decision) - **Why `role="alert"` alone is wrong:** `role="alert"` maps to `aria-live="assertive"`. Applying it to all three tiers forces Warning/Info notifications to interrupt the screen reader's current reading queue, breaking clinician workflow and violating WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages must be non-urgent unless critical). - **Three dedicated announcers:** - Critical: `
` → interrupts immediately, reads completely. - Warning: `
` → waits for polite queue to clear, reads completely. - Info: `
` → announces only new content added, does not read full message if user is already reading the panel. - **Injection pattern:** Never append DOM nodes to live regions. Use `clear → inject string → (optional 10ms delay)` pattern to prevent NVDA/JAWS race conditions with dynamic list rendering. --- ## Focus Management Plan 1. **Panel open:** Focus moves to `#close-panel-btn` (top of panel) per APG Dialog pattern. This provides an immediate escape path and matches standard dialog focus behavior. 2. **Focus trap:** When panel is open, Tab cycles within panel interactive elements. Shift+Tab on first element wraps to last. Background remains inert via `aria-modal="true"` + programmatic inert fallback for older browsers. 3. **Dismiss action focus movement:** - If dismissing a non-last notification: Focus moves to the next dismiss button in the list (`nextSibling.querySelector('button')?.focus()`). - If dismissing the last notification: Focus returns to `#bell-trigger` (the trigger element) per WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order and APG Dialog pattern. 4. **History drawer open:** Focus moves to first history item or `#close-history-btn`. Drawer is not modal; focus does not trap outside it, but panel remains open behind it. 5. **Focus indicators:** Default browser outlines are sufficient if they meet 3:1 contrast. Custom focus ring must use double-ring technique (`outline` + `box-shadow`) to remain visible on dark/light backgrounds. Use `:focus-visible` (not `:focus`). 6. **WCAG citations:** 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Appearance, APG Dialog/Popover patterns. --- ## State Communication Design ### State Communication Table | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------------| | Panel open/closed | Panel slides in/out, overlay appears | `hidden` attribute toggled, focus management | `aria-expanded` on trigger, `role="dialog"` on panel | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 2.4.3 Focus Order | | Badge count update | Numeric badge on bell icon | Dynamic `aria-label` update on button | `aria-label="Notifications, X unread"` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Critical notification arrives | Red banner/icon, bold text | Text injected into critical announcer | `aria-live="assertive"`, `aria-atomic="true"` | 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Warning notification arrives | Amber banner/icon, standard text | Text injected into warning announcer | `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"` | 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Info notification arrives | Blue banner/icon, muted text | Text injected into info announcer | `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-relevant="additions"` | 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Auto-dismiss paused | Toggle shows "Paused" state | `aria-pressed` toggled on control | `aria-pressed="true"` / `"false"` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable | | Dismiss in progress | Button shows spinner/loading state | `aria-disabled="true"` during async operation | `aria-disabled="true"` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | History drawer open | Drawer slides from side | `hidden` attribute toggled, landmark active | `aria-live="off"` on section | 4.1.3 Status Messages (explicitly off) | ### Badge Count Strategy - Update `aria-label` on `#bell-trigger` dynamically as WebSocket messages arrive: `aria-label="Notifications, 5 unread"`. - **Do NOT use a separate live region for badge increments.** Announcing "3", "4", "5" sequentially causes screen reader spam. - When panel is closed and a new notification arrives, the tiered announcer will speak the message. The bell button's `aria-label` update alone does not trigger an announcement unless the user focuses the button. This prevents unwanted interruptions during active EHR workflows. ### Auto-Dismis Timing (WCAG 2.2.1) - WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable requires pause/stop/hide controls for any auto-updating content with timeout < 20s. - **Requirement:** Add "Pause auto-dismiss" toggle button (`#pause-auto-dismiss-btn`). When pressed, all active timers pause indefinitely until resumed or panel closed. - Base timeouts must be configurable per institution policy. Default recommendation: Critical (never), Warning (60s minimum for AT compatibility), Info (30s minimum). 10s/30s defaults are insufficient for many screen reader users per WCAG 2.2.1. --- ## Visual Accessibility Plan 1. **Color contrast & non-color alternatives (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.1):** - Priority colors (red/amber/blue) must meet 3:1 against adjacent backgrounds for UI components and 4.5:1 for text. - Color alone MUST NOT indicate priority. Every notification requires: color border/icon + explicit text label ("CRITICAL", "WARNING", "INFO") + shape/icon indicator. 2. **Focus indicators (WCAG 2.4.7):** - Double-ring focus state on all buttons and list items. Minimum 3:1 contrast change between focused/unfocused states. Perimeter area ≥ 2px. - Use `outline` + `box-shadow` together. Apply via `:focus-visible`. 3. **Touch targets (WCAG 2.5.8):** - All interactive elements (bell button, dismiss buttons, history trigger, pause toggle) minimum 44x44 CSS pixels. 4. **Animation/motion (WCAG 2.3.3):** - Panel open/close and drawer slide must respect `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. Disable or reduce to <5ms transitions for AT users. 5. **Responsive text & zoom (WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.10):** - Use `rem`/`em` units. Test at 200% zoom: no horizontal scroll, content reflows vertically, touch targets remain ≥44px. --- ## Content Accessibility Plan 1. **Dismissible button labels (WCAG 2.4.4, 4.1.2):** - Pattern: `aria-label="Dismiss: [Priority] [Message Summary]"` - Example: `aria-label="Dismiss: Critical Lab Result — Patient Doe, John"` - Never use generic "X" or "Close" without context. Screen readers must announce what is being dismissed. 2. **Notification message clarity (WCAG 3.3.1):** - Messages must be concise but clinically complete. Avoid jargon where possible. Include patient name, test/order, value/status, and required action. 3. **Priority labeling:** - Explicit text labels ("CRITICAL", "WARNING", "INFO") alongside color/icon. Do not rely on `aria-label` alone for priority; it must be visible to low-vision users. 4. **Language attributes (WCAG 3.1.1):** - `` on root. If multilingual EHR, add `lang` attribute to notification text nodes dynamically. 5. **Reading order (WCAG 1.3.2):** - DOM order must match visual priority: Critical items first in the list, then Warning, then Info. Do not use CSS grid/flex reordering that breaks DOM sequence. --- ## Testing Strategy ### Testing Layer Architecture - **Static analysis:** `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` (CI gate) for JSX patterns, invalid ARIA, missing labels. - **Runtime scanning:** `axe-core` via Playwright injection for computed contrast, landmark structure, ARIA state correctness. - **Keyboard interaction:** Real Playwright key presses (`Tab`, `Enter`, `Escape`, `Arrow`) to validate focus trap, dismiss behavior, and panel open/close. - **Manual screen reader testing:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver validation of live region politeness, badge updates, and announcement timing. ### AT-Specific Test Cases | Test Case | Tool/Method | Pass Criteria | WCAG Citation | |-----------|-------------|---------------|---------------| | Critical notification arrives while panel closed | NVDA/JAWS | Announces immediately via assertive region. Interrupts current reading queue. | 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Warning notification arrives while panel open & user reading Info list | VoiceOver | Waits for polite queue to clear before announcing. Does not interrupt reading. | 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Badge count increments while panel closed | NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver | No announcement spam. `aria-label` updates on bell button. Focus button to verify label change. | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Dismiss non-last notification | Keyboard + Screen Reader | Focus moves to next dismiss button. Announcer speaks "Dismissed: [Priority] [Message]". | 2.4.3 Focus Order, 4.1.3 | | Dismiss last notification | Keyboard + Screen Reader | Focus returns to bell trigger. Panel remains open (or closes per UX spec). | 2.4.3 Focus Order | | Pause auto-dismiss toggle | Keyboard + Screen Reader | Toggle state announced ("Paused" / "Resumed"). Timers halt immediately. | 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable | | History drawer opens | Keyboard + Screen Reader | Focus moves to first item/close button. Region does NOT announce historical items (`aria-live="off"`). | 4.1.3 Status Messages, 2.4.3 | | 200% zoom layout | Visual/Playwright | No horizontal scroll. Touch targets ≥44px. Text readable without overflow. | 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 2.5.8 | ### Acceptance Criteria - All three priority tiers use separate `aria-live` regions with correct politeness levels. - No `role="alert"` used on notification elements or live regions. - Dismiss buttons are native `
